stem: Explain two ways in which believing that God is loving influences Christians today.
modelAnswer: Firstly, Christians try to love others. Because God loved the world so much that he sent his Son, they follow his example by caring for people in need, for example by giving to charities such as Christian Aid. Secondly, Christians trust God in difficult times. Believing that God loves them personally, they pray and feel comforted that God cares about what happens to them.

markScheme.text: First point: Christians try to love other people
Developed: because God loves them, they follow his example — e.g. "love your neighbour", helping the poor
Second point: Christians trust God in hard times
Developed: they believe God cares for them, so they pray and feel comforted when suffering

examinerNote: Each way needs a second sentence that develops it — usually "because…" or "for example…".

stem: Explain two Christian beliefs about the creation of the world. Refer to sacred writings or another source of Christian belief and teaching in your answer.
modelAnswer: Christians believe God created the world out of nothing. "In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth" (Genesis 1:1), and he saw that it was good, so Christians believe they should look after creation. Christians also believe the whole Trinity was involved. Genesis says the Spirit was "hovering over the waters", and John's gospel says of the Word, Jesus, "through him all things were made". So creation was the work of Father, Son and Holy Spirit together.

markScheme.text: First point: God created the world out of nothing (ex nihilo) and it is good
Developed: Genesis 1 shows God creating by his word, and seeing that it was good — so Christians should care for creation
Second point: all three persons of the Trinity were involved in creation
Developed: the Spirit "hovered over the waters" (Genesis 1:2) and the Word (Jesus) — "through him all things were made" (John 1:3)
Relevant sacred writing or source of authority, e.g. "In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth" (Genesis 1:1) or John 1:1-3

stem: "The existence of evil and suffering proves God is not loving." Evaluate this statement. In your answer you should give reasoned arguments to support this statement, give reasoned arguments to support a different point of view, refer to Christian teaching, and reach a justified conclusion.

levels.descriptor: A well-argued response with reasoned consideration of different points of view. Logical chains of reasoning lead to a justified conclusion, supported by accurate religious teaching.
indicativeContent: For: A loving, all-powerful God would stop suffering, so either God is not loving or not all-powerful (the inconsistent triad)
For: Natural disasters and disease are not caused by humans, so free will cannot explain them
For: Atheists and humanists argue the amount of suffering is too great for a loving God
Against: Free will: God loves us enough to let us choose; most suffering comes from humans misusing it
Against: Vale of soul-making (Hick): suffering helps people grow in compassion and courage
Against: God shared in suffering through Jesus on the cross — "God so loved the world" (John 3:16)
Against: Christians believe suffering will end in heaven, where God will "wipe every tear"
A conclusion that weighs the two sides and says which is stronger, and why

Second point: Muslims believe adultery is wrong
Developed: it is zina, a serious sin — "Do not go anywhere near adultery: it is an outrage" (17:32)

stem: Explain two contrasting Christian beliefs about violent protest.

markScheme.text: First point: most Christians believe protest must be peaceful
Developed: Jesus taught "turn the other cheek"; Martin Luther King Jr achieved civil rights through non-violent protest
Second point: a few Christians believe violence can sometimes be justified
Developed: "righteous anger" against serious injustice — Jesus overturned the tables of the traders in the Temple
